summary: The patch correctly adds self.save_m2m() to persist ManyToMany data, but does so in a second redundant `if commit:` block that calls user.save() a second time, so the user is saved twice. The fix should have added save_m2m() to the existing if-block instead.

issues.description: Wrong implementation: a duplicate `if commit:` block was appended instead of editing the existing one. Result is two consecutive `user.save()` calls, saving the user twice on every commit. Correct fix adds only `self.save_m2m()` to the existing block.

Behavioral regression: redundant second user.save() triggers extra signals (pre_save/post_save) and a second DB write/UPDATE on every UserCreationForm.save(commit=True), changing observable side-effect behavior.
Performance: avoidable duplicate database write per save() call.
Two identical adjacent `if commit:` blocks is unclear and clearly unintended structure.
